title: Adaptive stochastic paths and brownian bridge coupling

items.title: Dyadic Brownian bridge increment tree
items.statement: Given a parent Brownian increment over an interval of length h and an independent Gaussian midpoint innovation, split it into path-consistent left and right increments; retain the parent and stored children after rejection.

items.title: Exact increment laws in the dyadic Brownian bridge tree
items.statement: At each fixed dyadic depth, the tree increments are mutually independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance equal to their interval length times the identity; every parent equals the sum of its children.

items.title: Predictable stopping-time grid
items.statement: A finite random partition by stopping times whose next interval length is measurable at the current stopped sigma-algebra and is bounded by a deterministic maximum.

items.title: Continuous adapted processes are measurable at bounded stopping times
items.statement: On a usual augmented Brownian filtration, an adapted finite-dimensional process with almost surely continuous paths, evaluated at a bounded stopping time, is measurable at the stopped sigma-algebra.

items.title: Itô integral of a step on a stopping-time interval
items.statement: For stopping times tau<=sigma and an L2 coefficient measurable at F_tau, the predictable integrand xi 1_(tau,sigma] integrates to xi times the stopped Brownian increment.

items.title: Euler–Maruyama on a predictable grid with bridge-refinement status
items.statement: Use the Euler–Maruyama update on intervals selected from current stopped information, and use the saved bridge tree after endpoint-based rejection; finite budgets return complete or inconclusive status, with convergence asserted only on the predictable-grid branch. The filtered space satisfies the usual conditions and endpoint acceptance is a Borel function of finite history and trial data.

items.title: A finite adaptive Euler–Maruyama budget returns a status
items.statement: A work budget B in the adaptive Euler–Maruyama procedure yields at most B trial operations and returns complete exactly when the terminal time is reached; otherwise it returns inconclusive.

items.title: Uniform second moment for Euler–Maruyama on predictable grids
items.statement: Under global Lipschitz and linear-growth coefficient conditions, finite predictable meshes with maximum step at most T have a continuous Euler interpolation with uniformly bounded expected squared path supremum.

items.title: Strong error bound for Euler–Maruyama on a predictable grid
items.statement: For a finite predictable stopping-time mesh with step lengths bounded by deterministic 0<h<=T (one may take h=min{h_max,T}), global Lipschitz, linear-growth and half-Hölder-in-time coefficients give sup_t E|X_t-Y_t|^2 <= C h; a finite expected step-count claim is not inferred without a budget or E[N]<infinity.

items.title: Scalar Brownian bridge from x to y
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $h>0$, $x,y\in\mathbb R$, and let $W$ be a standard scalar
Brownian motion on $[0,h]$. The **scalar Brownian bridge from $x$ to $y$ over
duration $h$** is the continuous Gaussian process
$$B^{x,y,h}_t=x+\frac{t}{h}(y-x)+W_t-\frac{t}{h}W_h, \qquad 0\le t\le h.$$
It starts at $x$ and ends at $y$. Its law does not depend on which Brownian
motion is used: Brownian increment laws determine its finite-dimensional laws.
For the path-law assertion, give $C([0,h])$ the uniform topology and extend
each path $f$ by $E_hf(s)=f(s\wedge h)$ for $s\ge0$. This is a homeomorphism
onto the closed subspace of $C([0,\infty))$ consisting of paths constant
after $h$, with inverse restriction to $[0,h]$. Thus
[[lem-borel-sigma-algebra-of-continuous-path-space-is-generated-by-coordinates]]
makes the Borel sigma-algebra on $C([0,h])$ generated by its coordinates:
coordinates of the extension after $h$ equal $f(h)$, and continuity recovers
every coordinate, including $h$, from rational times in $[0,h]$.
Equality on finite coordinate cylinders now gives equality of path laws by
[[thm-dynkin-pi-lambda]]. The endpoint-conditional and restriction-density
properties are established separately on the A page.

items.title: Endpoint law and restriction density of a scalar Brownian bridge
items.statement: For fixed endpoint y and t<h, the bridge path law up to time t is absolutely continuous with respect to Brownian motion from x, with density p_(h-t)(y-W_t)/p_h(y-x).

items.title: Scalar Brownian bridge barrier-crossing probability
items.statement: For x,y>=c and h>0, a scalar Brownian bridge from x to y crosses the level c with probability exp(-2(x-c)(y-c)/h), including probability one when either endpoint equals c.

title: Adaptive stochastic paths and brownian bridge coupling — Examples

items.title: Redrawing a rejected Brownian increment biases the path
items.statement: Conditioning or repeatedly resampling a Gaussian increment after an endpoint-based rejection changes its law; bridge-tree refinement preserves the already drawn parent path.

items.title: Coarse and fine Euler paths coupled by a bridge split
items.statement: A one-step coarse Euler path and two-step fine Euler path share a parent Brownian increment through its bridge children, with an explicit nonzero difference for the linear drift b(x)=x.

items.title: A Brownian bridge can cross a barrier missed by its endpoints
items.statement: A bridge with both endpoints above a level has positive crossing probability; for endpoints 1 and 1, level 0 and duration 1 the probability is exp(-2).
